REQ-1-1-1-API-AUTH-ROUTES.content: {"interface_id": "REQ-1-1-1-API-AUTH-ROUTES", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "API", "name": "authRoutes (POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/session, POST /api/auth/logout)", "file_path": "backend/src/routes/auth_routes.js", "first_line": "const express = require('express');", "responsibility": "HTTP surface for registration, sign-in, durable session recovery and sign-out; mounted at /api/auth and delegating all rules to the auth service.", "specification": "POST /register body { username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms } -> 201 { user: { id, username, email, emailVerified: true }, session: { token } } and sets the httpOnly session cookie; 400 { fieldErrors } carrying every violated field at once; 409 { fieldErrors } for username/email conflicts with messages 'Username already exists' / 'Email already exists'. REQ-1-1-1-FUNC-AUTH-SERVICE.content: {"interface_id": "REQ-1-1-1-FUNC-AUTH-SERVICE", "req_id": "REQ-1-1-1", "type": "FUNC", "name": "authService (validateRegistrationInput, registerAccount, authenticateUser, session helpers, ensureSeedAccount)", "file_path": "backend/src/services/auth_service.js", "first_line": "'use strict';", "responsibility": "Owns registration/credential business rules: username and email format rules, password composition rules, uniqueness enforcement, verified-email account creation, password hashing, credential verification, durable session records, and the idempotent seed account.", "specification": "validateRegistrationInput collects ALL violated fields at once keyed by field name. Username: 1-39 lowercase ASCII letters/digits/single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen (USERNAME_PATTERN). Email: trimmed, exactly one '@', length <= 254, at least one dot and non-empty labels after '@'. Password: 12-128 chars, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit, one non-alphanumeric, no whitespace. Confirmation must match. Terms must be accepted. registerAccount returns { ok: true, user } after inserting a sign-in-capable row with email_verified = 1, or { ok: false, fieldErrors } with FIELD_MESSAGES.usernameExists / emailExists for conflicts and never a partially created account. authenticateUser accepts either usable identifier (username or email) plus the password and returns the public user. createSession/loadSessionUser/destroySession persist and resolve opaque tokens in the sessions table so GET /session survives reload. ensureSeedAccount idempotently upserts the scenario seed account ('alice-dev', 'alice.dev@example.test', 'Valid-password-123!', email_verified = 1) through db_runtime with INSERT OR IGNORE/upsert semantics and is safe to call repeatedly. All persistence goes through backend/src/database/db_runtime.js helpers; never secrets or plaintext passwords are returned. Body currently throws explicit not-implemented errors — TDD implements them.", "inputs": "Registration/credential/session inputs from the route layer; no direct HTTP access.", "outputs": "Typed results: { ok, user | fieldErrors }, public user projections, session tokens, and void for seed/logout.", "callers": [], "callees": [], "test_focus": ["unit tests per rule: invalid username with leading hyphen, 'not-an-email', 'short'/'different' password, unchecked terms all reported together", "duplicate username with a fresh email reports 'Username already exists' and creates nothing", "successful registration stores a verified email and never returns the password or hash", "authenticateUser succeeds for the newly registered account and for the seeded account", "ensureSeedAccount is idempotent across repeated runs"]}
